faults.title: The search-sync drain batch was a live control, so a hand step of search_sync.batch looked like a tuning lever on prod while the OpenSearch write pool was the limit

The measured drain was 2,636 rows/s at 5000 and 2,352 rows/s at 10000 (6 x 120 s), with the OpenSearch write pool at 72/72 active, queue 18, 0 rejected, so a bigger batch did not help. Commit 3b01d8026 deletes the search_sync.batch control: the drain and the backfill feed read SEARCH_SYNC_BATCH = 5,000 from apps/crawler-v3/src/index/tuning.py, and PATCH /ops/config refuses the key (tests/unit/test_search_sync_batch.py). exempt.config_reason_regex: ^owner: "|A/B|live-ab W\d|^Owner order|the owner's order of \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}: '|owner (?:ruling|rule) on (?:todo )?t\d+|^Owner's [^(]{0,60}\(todo t\d+
exempt.note: An owner order quoted in the reason or opened with 'Owner order', or a named A/B experiment with its restore, is a decision, not a hand fix, and so is the restore row of a named live-ab window (audit 14869, proxy.connect_racers back to 20 after live-ab W1 on 10-19). The staging `.venv/bin/python - 3600 8` exec and the prod `python -c "$0"` exec of the script that opens 'Daily B2 version inventory for ONE bucket' are the declared unit virev-b2-inventory.service (host.yml --tags b2-inventory, its timer; on prod run-inventory.sh calls inventory.py host influencer-prod virev-prod-crawler-worker, read 10-18 05:34Z), so neither is a hand-started process. A board note on a d3 run or the d3 precheck reports this duty's own work, not a hand fix. A reason that quotes the owner's dated order (the owner's order of 2026-10-13: 'can we not enrich for now?', pause.enrich audit 14089) is the same kind of decision, and so is a reason that cites the owner's answer on a For you todo by id ('owner ruling on todo t61', 'owner rule on t65', 'Owner's fixed census cap (todo t67, c170)', audits 16761, 16777 and 16768 on 10-26). A key named in config_key_regex is a lane's fixed cap that owner rule c170 (10-26) has operators set by hand from measured good reads, so a change that writes only such keys is design, not a hand fix. meta_ads.walker_sessions_max is the one operator cap a climb knob reads (crawler-v3 control/climb.py top_key); prod audit 16886 set it to 360 on 10-28 03:51Z and read as F1. A write to meta_ads.walker_sessions itself still counts as F1.
exempt.box_exec_regex: \.venv/bin/python - 3600 8$|Daily B2 version inventory for ONE bucket
